blocks.etymology: Attested 1825; Unadapted borrowing from French troupe, which see for more. Doublet of troop, and possibly also of thorp and dorp.

wiktionary.gloss: To tour with a troupe.

blocks.etymology: From under- + bred.

thesaurus.definition: (of persons) lacking in refinement or grace

vi_block: Kém giáo dục, vô giáo dục, thô lỗ, thô tục.

wiktionary.gloss: Of inferior breeding or upbringing; vulgar, lacking in manners or finesse.
Not purebred; of an inferior strain.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English upshiften, upschyften (“to raise”), equivalent to up- + shift.

examples: You can upshift to second gear once the car is moving.
wiktionary.gloss: To shift to a higher gear.

examples: The frequency of the light is upshifted.
wiktionary.gloss: To shift to a higher level, such as of frequency, growth rate, economic level, etc.

blocks.etymology: The adjective (then also used as a participle) is first attested in 1420, in Middle English, the verb in 1620; partly from Middle English vibrat(e) (“reverberant”), partly directly borrowed from Latin vibrātus, perfect passive participle of vibrō (“to agitate, set in tremulous motion”) (see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyp- (“to oscillate, swing”) or *weyb-.

senses.definition: to shake continuously with very small, quick movements, or to cause something to do this

examples.en: The phone started to vibrate on the table.
examples.vi: Chiếc điện thoại bắt đầu rung trên bàn.

examples.en: Loud music made the windows vibrate.
examples.vi: Tiếng nhạc lớn làm các ô cửa sổ rung lên.

senses.definition: to be filled with excitement, strong energy, or deep sound

examples.en: The room was vibrating with intense energy.
examples.vi: Căn phòng rộn ràng với nguồn năng lượng cuồng nhiệt.

thesaurus.definition: shake, quiver, or throb; move back and forth rapidly, usually in an uncontrolled manner
move or swing from side to side regularly
be undecided about something; waver between conflicting positions or courses of action
sound with resonance
feel sudden intense sensation or emotion

vi_block: Rung lên, ngân vang lên (âm thanh).

wiktionary.gloss: To shake with small, rapid movements to and fro.

examples: Her mind was vibrating with excitement.
wiktionary.gloss: To resonate.

examples: to vibrate a sword or a staff
wiktionary.gloss: To brandish; to swing to and fro.

examples: a pendulum vibrating seconds
wiktionary.gloss: To mark or measure by moving to and fro.
To affect with vibratory motion; to set in vibration.
To please or impress someone.
To use vibrato.
To pleasure someone using a vibrator.

blocks.etymology: The adjective (then also used as a participle) is first attested in 1420, in Middle English, the verb in 1620; partly from Middle English vibrat(e) (“reverberant”), partly directly borrowed from Latin vibrātus, perfect passive participle of vibrō (“to agitate, set in tremulous motion”) (see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyp- (“to oscillate, swing”) or *weyb-.

senses.definition: a setting on a phone or electronic device that causes it to shake instead of ringing

examples.en: I put my phone on vibrate during the meeting.
examples.vi: Tôi để điện thoại ở chế độ rung trong suốt cuộc họp.

examples: Please put your cellphones on vibrate for the duration of the meeting.
wiktionary.gloss: The setting, on a portable electronic device, that causes it to vibrate rather than sound any (or most) needed alarms.
